title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two independent parts.

(1) Crossed-out group-theoretic scratch (top). There is an exact sequence 1 → N → G → 𝔊 → 1. The kernel is identified with N ≅ ((F_2)^A)' = Ker(F_2^A → F_2, (x_i) ↦ Σx_i): the 'sum-zero' (even) vectors in F_2^A, where A is a finite set on which 𝔊 acts by permutations. A complement 𝔊_0 (drawn with a curved arrow back into G) is used to write each element as g = u·x = y·u, with u ∈ 𝔊_0, x ∈ N and y = u x u^{-1} = u(x). Grothendieck then checks the multiplication law of the semidirect product in both normal forms:
- g'g = u'x'ux = (u'u)(u^{-1}(x')·x) = U''X'';
- equivalently g'g = y'u'yu'^{-1}u'u = (y'·u'(y))·u'u.
So G ≅ N ⋊ 𝔊_0 with the permutation action. When 𝔊 = S_A this group is the Weyl group W(D_n). Such groups arise as Galois or monodromy groups of the fields obtained by adjoining square roots of linear factors, e.g. 2-division and 'sqrt(e_i − e_j)' phenomena. The computations are correct and routine.

(2) Normality of the integral model of a quadratic extension of Q(t) (main text). This continues the previous and next pages ('normalité des extensions quadratiques').
- Setup: a quadratic extension of Q(t) is given by a normalized representative P = ±q·Q of Q(t)*/Q(t)*², where q is a squarefree integer and Q ∈ Z[t] is primitive, squarefree over Q, with positive leading coefficient (normal form from p.154). Take A = Z[t] and B = A[S]/(S² − P).
- Odd primes: for p odd, localize at the height-one prime pA. Then A(p) = A_{pA} = Z_{(p)}{t} is a DVR with residue field F_p(t).
  - If p | q, then P ∈ m∖m², an Eisenstein-type case, so B(p) is regular.
  - If p ∤ q, then P is a unit and 2 is invertible, so B(p) is étale over A(p).
  - Either way B(p) is normal.
- The prime p = 2:
  - If 2 | q, B(2) is normal.
  - If 2 ∤ q, P is a unit. B(2) is normal if P mod 2 is not a square in F_2(t), equivalently in F_2[t].
  - If P mod 2 is a square but P is not a square mod 4, it is still normal. This is the invariant b̃ ∈ m/m² of p.154, writing P = α² − b.
  - The only non-normal case is 2 ∤ q with ±Q a square mod 4. Examples are Q = t² − 4 ≡ t², and something like 4εt + 1 ≡ 1 (reading uncertain). In that case (S − α)/2 satisfies X² + αX + b/4 = 0, so it is integral but not in B.
- Horizontal primes: at height-one primes (f(t)) with f primitive irreducible, the residue characteristic is 0 and P is squarefree over Q, so B is normal there.
- Grothendieck's conclusion: apart from the exceptional case, B is normal in codimension 1. Its non-normal points are closed, hence isolated, so B is the normalization of the affine line E^1_Z = Spec Z[t] in the quadratic extension, except over a finite subscheme. Over Z[1/2] this holds with no exception.

The purpose is to describe integral models of double covers of the (affine/projective) line over Z. These are relevant to Legendre/λ-type families and level-2 structures in the study of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: Understatement, not a real error: B = A[S]/(S² − P) is a hypersurface in a 3-dimensional regular ring, hence Cohen–Macaulay and so S2. B is also reduced at the generic point, and the page establishes R1 by checking all height-one primes (vertical and horizontal). By Serre's criterion, B is then normal everywhere. The hedge 'non-normal points are closed, hence isolated, so B is the normalization except over a finite subscheme' is therefore unnecessary: outside the exceptional 2-adic case B is exactly the normalization, with no finite exceptional set.
In the exceptional case (2 ∤ q, ±Q a square mod 4) the non-normal locus is not isolated: it contains the generic point of the whole fibre over 2.
'Carré mod 4' should be understood in A_{(2)}/4, with the sign ± and the choice of α taken into account. The invariant b̃ ∈ m/m² is independent of α, as p.154 notes, so the criterion itself is fine.

ideas.what: Semidirect product N ⋊ 𝔊_0 with N the sum-zero subgroup of F_2^A, permutation action; verification of the multiplication law in both normal forms u·x and y·u
ideas.modern_name: Even-sign wreath-type group (F_2^A)_0 ⋊ 𝔊; W(D_n) when 𝔊 = S_n

ideas.what: Normality criterion for B = A[S]/(S² − P) over the DVRs A_{pA}, with the 2-adic subtlety: non-normal iff P is a unit square mod 4
ideas.modern_name: Integral closure of quadratic orders / normality of double covers in residue characteristic 2 (Artin–Schreier-type reduction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical commutative algebra (Dedekind discriminant considerations; standard in textbooks)

ideas.what: Normal form ±q·Q for Q(t)*/Q(t)*² and the integral model of the corresponding double cover of the affine line over Z, normal away from 2 and (generically) at 2
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of A^1_Z (or P^1_Z) in a quadratic extension; integral models of hyperelliptic/double covers

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine scratch: a semidirect-product multiplication check and an elementary normality analysis of quadratic extensions of Z[t], with the expected 2-adic subtlety. Nothing here is absent from the literature; the only remark is that Serre's criterion would strengthen the conclusion.
transcription_corrections: The exact sequence is 1 → N → G → 𝔊 → 1. The kernel is N (with x ∈ N later), and it is N that is identified with ((F_2)^A)' = Ker(F_2^A → F_2); A is the index set, not the kernel.

In the 2-adic discussion the divisibility conditions appear swapped in the transcription. The mathematically correct reading, which the image also seems to show, is: 'B(2) est normal si 2|q. Si 2∤q, il est normal aussi si Q mod 2 n'est pas un carré…' and 'le seul cas où B(2) ne soit [pas] normal est celui où 2∤q et Q(t) est un carré mod 4'.
X'' = u^{-1}(x')x, where u^{-1}(x') = u^{-1}x'u. The final line reads g'g = (y'·u'(y))·u'u.
'E'_Z' is most likely E^1_Z, the affine line over Z, consistent with Spec A = Spec Z[t] and with 'cas des E^1_Z' on p.154.
The second example is uncertain; it looks like Q(t) = 4εt + 1 (ε = ±1), i.e. a polynomial ≡ 1 mod 4, rather than '4t^ε + 1'.
